walkthroughs.body_html:
Foundations in Chemistry — a core area of A-Level Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Foundations in Chemistry brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Foundations in Chemistry.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Members of a homologous series share:
options: The same molecular mass
The same functional group and general formula
The same boiling point
The same number of isomers

mcqs.q: Why can transition metals show variable oxidation states?
options: Transition metals have variable oxidation states because they have many shells of electrons.
The 4s and 3d orbitals are similar in energy, so different numbers of electrons can be removed without a large energy cost.
A reaction with negative delta G must be exothermic in every case.
Transition metals have variable oxidation states because they can gain protons easily.

mcqs.q: Why does the colour of a transition metal complex change when ligands are exchanged?
options: The colour changes because the new ligand is itself coloured.
Different ligands cause different amounts of d-orbital splitting, so different wavelengths of light are absorbed.
Transition metals have variable oxidation states because they can gain protons easily.
The colour changes because the metal ion itself changes oxidation state.

mcqs.q: If a reaction has a negative Gibbs free energy change, what does that mean?
options: Transition metals have variable oxidation states because they can gain protons easily.
The reaction is thermodynamically feasible — it can proceed — but it may still be very slow.
A reaction with negative delta G must be exothermic in every case.
A reaction with negative delta G will always happen quickly.
